assets.statement: L1-as-branch-B-evidence fails: Maynard bound is subsequence-only (hidden-subsequence attack) and does not match the quantifier reversal of o(log N) (needs all-N failure at positive density, not infinitely many N); repair = uniform c·log N lower bound on the full primes, an equivalent-strength open p

REFUTED by external audit (GPT gold-mine audit + R4, 2026-09-01), each item re-verified by the operator's session against the frozen contract or by exact computation on 2026-09-02 | FALSE: Pintz/Rankin-type results concern LARGE GAPS between consecutive primes, not the length of arithmetic progressions of primes in [1,N]. No theorem gives L(N) = omega(log N) infinitely often; the longest known prime APs in [1,N] have length far below log N and the o(log N) question is open. 'negative close achieved' is a citation misuse.

refuted at smallest parameters: r=2, k=2 family I₁={2,3}, I₂={24,25} gives total product 3600=60², exactly verified; Pell a(a+1)=6t² yields infinitely many length-2 square-product blocks, so k=2 imposes no obstruction and any close must use a fixed r across all k≥2 with explicit integrality.

L1 ("all positive integers are sums of ≤3 2-full numbers") refuted by n=7: powerful ≤7 are {1,4}, 3-term sums miss 7 (also n=15); canonical "large" hedge is load-bearing, so any close needs an explicit threshold/exception set.
positive upper density does not imply positive natural density (explicit block-set counterexample); repair: prove a uniform lower bound |S_C∩[1,N]| ≥ δN for all large N, never a limsup.

certificate void as stated (explicit scope absent); under the only reading derivable from L1 (<=3 disjoint blocks of >=2 consecutive integers, elements <=20, k=2) the box contains exact squares 1*2*8*9=144=12^2, 4*5*8*9*10=14400=120^2, 3*4*5*6*9*10=32400=180^2, and the universal forall-r clause is r
